speaker: melissamarsh
text: Staff was requested to create the human relations and equity commission and a separate task force. The human relations and equity commission would duplicate much of the objectives of both the existing crime commission and the multicultural board. Therefore, this resolution would create a new human relations and equity commission with two other agenda items to dissolve the crime commission and multicultural advisory board. The human relations and equity commission would be advisory to the city council. They would recommend programs, policies, and activities that promote positive human relations and equitable outcomes and opportunities in all aspects of community life. The commission would consist of five voting members who are residents of Madison Heights and represent a diverse population. Ex officio member would be one city council member. The city manager, police chief, and or other staff may attend meetings in an advisory capacity to staff and the commission to offer direction and administrative services. Applicants should detail their interest and or experience and shall apply for either the chair or the general member position. Further, the police department is in the process of working towards a professional accreditation through the Michigan Law Enforcement Accreditation Commission. This program consists of 108 best practices across all areas of policing. Through this program, we must implement the best practices and prove we have been adhering to these policies and practices. After the proof has been gathered and submitted to the accreditation commission, a group of auditors will review all of the policies and proofs of attaining the standards, including record and call review and physical inspections. This process will be ongoing through December and possibly into early next year. Once the audit is completed, we will be given a report with findings that includes community-specific programs and concerns. Findings from this evaluation shall be given to the city council and shared with the Human Relation and Equity Commission. A task force of law enforcement and legal professionals shall be created to review this report and supplemental findings based on Madison Heights specific needs. If council concurs with the recommendation, the appropriate motion would be to approve the resolution to create the Human Relation and Equity Commission and subsequent task force. As a reminder, approval of this commission will also require the city council to approve the resolution and ordinance to combine the Crown Commission and Multicultural Board into the Human Relations and Equity Commission.
